description: Get one inventory item by id: name, description, status, category and its four relations (home location, current location, current holder, responsible person) with resolved names. It is also the tool that SHOWS one item: it returns `photoUrl`, the item's main photo (absent when it has none), and in hosts that render widgets it draws the item as a card — so call it when your user wants to SEE a single item ("show me the beamer", "what does BM-002 look like?") instead of narrating a search row back at them or drawing a card of your own out of photo-less rows. For several items at once, show_items draws the picker. `status` describes the item's CONDITION (available = not defect/lost/retired); a status-available item may still be borrowed — check `currentHolder`, or use check_item_availability. Packed items (see pack_item) additionally carry `container` plus `effectiveLocation`/`effectiveHolder` — the position followed from the container while the item's own currentLocation/currentHolder are empty — and `compartment` { id, name } when they sit in one of the container's compartments (a named spot inside it, e.g. a vehicle's «GR4»; absent = directly in the container). Container items carry `holdsItems: true`, `compartments` [{ id, name }] in their order when they have any (the names pack_item's `compartment` takes), `contentsCount`, and `packedStock` when quantity-tracked stock sits inside them: [{ itemId, name, primaryCode?, quantity, compartmentName? }]. A quantity-tracked item whose units sit inside containers carries `packed`: one row per container and compartment { containerId, containerName, containerPath?, compartmentName?, quantity, effectiveLocationName?, effectiveHolderName? } — its `quantity` total counts them. This is also the ONLY tool that returns the item's CUSTOM FIELD VALUES — serial number, warranty, purchase price, whatever the organization defined — as `customFields`, one entry per stored value with the org's own `label`, its `type`, the `value`, and `fieldDefId` to join it to the definitions get_item_requirements returns; a `date` value carries `valueIso`, the plain calendar day, and a `currency` value its `currencyCode` (absent = CHF). Ask here for "what's the serial number of X?", and call it after create_item / update_item to read back what actually landed. Values the connected user may not see are simply absent — restricted fields are invisible, not redacted. Search rows deliberately carry none of this: it is one item's detail, not list content. Drafts (unreviewed captures) are strictly personal: another user's draft is not found even by id (standard not-found) until it is published.
name: get_item
title: Get item
